issues.description: Fixed an issue where the firewall's certificate verification logic did not support the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm, which prevented proper validation of certificates using this algorithm. With this fix, the firewall can verify certificates signed with RSASSA-PSS. RSASSA-PSS support is disabled by default. Use the following operational mode command to enable it on each firewall: set system setting ssl-decrypt support-rsa-pss > no disable (default) > yes enable
Fixed an issue where frequent session failures occurred due to CTD resource exhaustion.

Fixed an issue where Cloud Identity Engine did not fetch user-mapping details for XML API users. This occurred when the firewall learned the same IP-user mapping multiple times within a short period. With this fix, the Cloud Identity Engine now accurately fetches these user-mapping details.
Fixed an issue where the traffic log user interface displayed an error when accessed. With this fix, the traffic log user interface functions as expected.

Fixed an issue where Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs) deployed in China could not establish trust for necessary Certificate Authority (CA) certificates, which prevented the fetching of device certificates. With this fix, Next-Generation Firewalls can now successfully obtain these certificates.

(PA-7000 Series firewalls only) Fixed an issue where you could not delete core files from the Line Card Processor (LFP) using the Command Line Interface (CLI). This occurred when you attempted to remove them. With this fix, you can now successfully remove these core files.

Fixed an issue where the firewall placed UDP sessions into a *Discard* state when a DNS Sinkhole/Block action occurred, which prevented subsequent DNS requests from reusing the same session and caused DNS-related outages.
Fixed an issue where the `debug management-server max-ref-xpaths 8000` CLI command was not applied automatically and required a *configd* process restart for the configuration to take effect.
Fixed an issue where a memory leak occurred when processing device and vsys tags.
Fixed an issue where repeated unexpected terminations of a system component would cause the Data Plane to restart. With this fix, the Data Plane maintained stability.

Fixed an issue where the DNS proxy would intermittently stop resolving DNS queries, which prevented users from accessing the internet, and which was observed during periods of high CPU utilization for the dnsproxy process. With this fix, the DNS proxy consistently resolves queries, ensuring reliable internet access.

Fixed an issue where a website would intermittently fail to load in Mozilla Firefox after authentication when AURL inline cloud was active, which was caused by an interaction with the inline cloud analysis process. With this fix, websites now load consistently.
Fixed an issue where the `debug management-server max-ref-xpaths 8000` CLI command was not applied automatically, and a *configd* process restart was required for the change to take effect.

Fixed an issue where an additional routing table entry was unexpectedly created with a next hop that would discard traffic, appearing in the routing table after a short period. With this fix, such unexpected entries are no longer created.

Fixed an issue where Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peering over an IPv6-only interface did not correctly support RFC 5549 (IPv4 over IPv6 Next Hops), which resulted in advertised IPv4 routes using the router-ID as the next hop instead of an IPv6 next hop. With this fix, BGP correctly advertises IPv4 routes with IPv6 next hops when peering over an IPv6-only interface.

Fixed an issue where packets that had completed processing would not be sent out, which occurred because an internal optimization mechanism did not properly flush the transmit queue under certain traffic conditions. With this fix, packets are consistently transmitted.

Fixed an issue where the Panorama user interface incorrectly reported that master nodes were not running on all nodes in an Elastic Search (ES) cluster, which occurred because all log collectors in a collector group were incorrectly selected as master eligible nodes by default after a Panorama upgrade. With this fix, the Panorama user interface accurately reflects the status of master nodes.

($$VM-Series firewalls in AWS environments configured with IMDSv2 only$$) Fixed an issue where Elastic Network Interface (ENI) IDs were not displayed by a diagnostic command, which occurred when Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) was the only metadata service enabled for the instance. With this fix, the command now correctly displays ENI IDs.
Fixed an issue on Panorama where exporting managed device information that included a PA-450R-5G appliance resulted in the **Cellular Firmware** field being exported into multiple cells.

Fixed an issue where WildFire Analysis reports failed to load, displaying a **500 Internal Server Error** when the system attempted to retrieve reports for certain files. With this fix, WildFire Analysis reports load as expected.
Fixed an issue where the console became enabled after a reboot on a firewall operating in FIPSCC mode. With this fix, the console remains disabled across reboots when FIPSCC mode is active.

Fixed an issue where the firewall did not generate certain system SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) traps, such as those with system trap IDs 989855745 and 989855746, including "panROUTINGRouted…" traps (for example, "panROUTINGRoutedPIMNeighborDisappearedTrap") and "panSSLVPNSslvpn…" traps (for example, "panSSLVPNSslvpnRegistSuccTrap"), because of a defect in the PAN-TRAPS MIB. With this fix, the firewall generates these traps as expected.
Fixed an issue where ACC logs displayed a discrepancy in SSL traffic information between Panorama and the firewall. With this fix, the SSL traffic information in ACC logs now aligns correctly.

Fixed an issue where, after upgrading an LSVPN portal/gateway to an affected release, the portal was unable to issue and transfer certificates to the satellite firewalls, which led to repeated certificate requests and prevented the satellite firewalls from authenticating to the gateway.

(PA-3420 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the explicit proxy service would unexpectedly terminate when processing Kerberos authentication bypass traffic over extended periods. With this fix, the explicit proxy service maintains stability under these conditions.

($$AIRS firewalls on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments only$$) Fixed an issue where the firewall displayed a Kubernetes cluster ID of 0 in the traffic logs in SCM when traffic was denied for Kubernetes workloads, even though the traffic zone was correctly identified with the corresponding non-zero cluster ID.
Fixed an issue where SSL syslog forwarding did not work with CRL or OCSP check enabled with a management IPv6 address with a **::** character.
Fixed an issue where a memory leak would occur, which led to increased memory utilization. With this fix, memory resources are managed efficiently.

(PA-VM KVM firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the Data Handling Agent (DHA) process crashed after an IPv6 address was configured on a loopback interface, High Availability was enabled, and the firewall was rebooted.
Fixed an issue where the *logrcvr* process on a firewall stopped responding due to a document node being unexpectedly freed.

Fixed an issue where some FQDNs could not be resolved by the firewall. This occurred even when your configured Domain Name System (DNS) servers successfully returned valid IP addresses for the FQDNs. With this fix, the firewall correctly processes DNS responses and resolves FQDNs as expected.

Added a debug CLI command to address where remote networks for Prisma Access tenants randomly dropped monitoring packets from peer devices, which caused tunnels to be marked as down. This occurred when a CPU core suddenly experienced high utilization. To utilize this fix, run `debug dataplane set ssl-decrypt use-new-peek-window yes`.

# PUBLIC SUMMARY (Panorama appliances in Log Collector mode only) Fixed an issue where the log collectors became unstable for an extended period of time when receiving large amounts of traffic. # COPILOT DETAILS ## AFFECTED PLATFORMS Panorama appliances in Log Collector mode only ## FIX VERSIONS Not yet resolved ## DESCRIPTION M-600 Log Collectors running PAN-OS 11.1.4-h26 experienced Elasticsearch (ES) cluster instability under high log ingestion rates. This manifested as `ProcessClusterEventTimeoutException` and `writing cluster state took [61828ms]` messages in `__pan_cluster.log`, `ELASTICSEARCH STATUS: status is red!` and high `number_of_pending_tasks` in `esmonitor.log`, and `UNASSIGNED SHARD REASON: NODE_LEFT` in ES analysis, indicating a failure to process cluster events and manage shards effectively. This led to the Log Collector group becoming destabilized. ## SYMPTOMS * Log Collector health status flapping. * Elasticsearch cluster health status reported as "red". * Presence of unassigned shards in Elasticsearch. * `esmonitor.log` shows `ELASTICSEARCH STATUS: status is red!` and high `number_of_pending_tasks`. * `__pan_cluster.log` contains `ProcessClusterEventTimeoutException` and `writing cluster state took [61828ms]` warnings. * `es-analysis` output shows `UNASSIGNED SHARD REASON: NODE_LEFT`. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER The issue occurred on M-600 Log Collectors after upgrading to PAN-OS 11.1.4-h26 when the devices received high peaks of traffic, specifically log ingestion rates exceeding typical limits (e.g., 100,000 logs per second). ## IMPACT The Log Collector group became destabilized for extended periods, leading to potential delays in log processing, log visibility issues, and overall operational disruption. The Elasticsearch cluster's unhealthy state could also impact log querying capabilities.
Fixed an issue where pushing multiple policy rules failed when the policy rules contained a large number of dynamic address object groups or user groups.

($$Panorama appliances on Google Cloud Platform only$$) Fixed an issue where administrators could not establish an SSH connection to Panorama using `ed25519` keys. With this fix, `ed25519` keys are now supported for SSH access.
Fixed an issue where the *mgmt* process stopped responding after an upgrade during SSH Key Exchange verification.

Fixed an issue where firewalls using the Real-Time update setting for WildFire intermittently generated system alerts indicating a failure to connect to the WildFire real-time cloud. With this fix, these alerts are no longer generated.

Fixed an issue where an internal interface identifier became invalid following real-time threat analysis processing. This caused traffic to be misrouted or improperly handled. With this fix, the system correctly manages interface identifiers during threat analysis, ensuring consistent traffic flow.
Fixed an issue on the Panorama web interface where refreshing or configuring settings in the **Response Pages** tab caused the web interface to respond more slowly when navigating to other tabs.

Fixed a rare issue on Octeon Dataplane platforms where the firewall experienced an unexpected dataplane restart due to a race condition that occurred during session teardown for traffic undergoing software-based Content Threat detection.

Fixed an issue on Panorama where a database component unexpectedly stopped when Panorama was deployed using an .ova file or upgraded/downgraded to an affected PAN-OS version. This occurred due to a required directory not being created during the initial provisioning workflow. With this fix, the necessary directory is created automatically during deployment.

(PA-3440 firewalls in Active/Active High Availability (HA) configuration only) Fixed an issue where one firewall would not install Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) learned routes into the routing table, particularly after OSPF Designated Router (DR) and Backup Designated Router (BDR) elections, which could lead to routing inconsistencies between the HA peers. With this fix, both firewalls consistently install OSPF learned routes.

Fixed an issue where changing the High Availability (HA) passive link status mode through the user interface (UI) failed to apply the configuration. With this fix, the UI correctly updates the passive link status.
Fixed an issue where customized destination pages displayed content improperly formatted. With this fix, customized destination pages display content correctly.

Fixed an issue where Inline Cloud Analyzer (ICA) did not correctly apply custom URL categories configured as exceptions for traffic detection. With this fix, ICA correctly applies the configured custom URL category exceptions.

Fixed an issue where the firewall stripped the Authentication Key Identifier (AKID) from certificates using SSL decryption, which prevented clients from authenticating server certificates and resulted in decryption failures.

($$Firewalls in HA active/active configurations only$$) Fixed an issue where the firewall experienced random reboots due to a memory leak in the *ikemgr* process triggered by configuration pushes. The leak occurred when an IKE Gateway was configured on a loopback interface using a floating IP address, leading to repeated socket bind failures on the secondary device.

Fixed an issue where the *device-telemetry collect-now* process became unresponsive when the process was initiated multiple times with other processes running concurrently, which prevented subsequent telemetry collection.
Fixed an issue on Panorama where a system health check Security policy rule was applied to **any** zones instead of **Public** or **Private**.
Fixed an issue on Panorama where scheduled Saas Application usage reports and on-demand reports generated using **Run Now** displayed different results.

Fixed an issue on Panorama where, when an Aggregate Ethernet interface was configured in override mode within a template stack, changing its management profile unexpectedly overrode other interface-specific variables.

Fixed an issue where system processes would unexpectedly terminate on Prisma Access instances during a configuration commit operation when TLS 1.3 proxy settings were configured. With this fix, system processes remain stable during configuration commits.

Fixed an issue where the Advanced WildFire cloud status would show as disconnected after a software upgrade, which prevented the firewall from maintaining a connection to the service. With this fix, the firewall properly maintained its connection to the Advanced WildFire cloud.

($$Firewalls in FIPS mode only$$) Fixed decryption issues that occurred after an upgrade to an affected release. To enable this fix, run the CLI command `debug dataplane set ssl-decrypt low-memory-throttle enable`.
Fixed an issue where API responses included an unexpected NUL character when retrieved using API clients, which interfered with the processing of the response.
Fixed an issue where, during a commit, the firewall intermittently stopped sending SNMP messages, which caused interface counters to stop updating for brief periods of time.
($$Firewalls in active/passive HA configurations only$$) Fixed an issue where the Clientless VPN applications failed to load due to the firewall dataplane incorrectly processing session information.
Fixed an issue where committing a scheduled configuration push on Panorama caused the *configd* process to stop responding unexpectedly.

Fixed an issue where a TLSv1.3 handshake did not complete when SSL Forward Proxy was enabled. This occurred when a large ClientHello message was split across multiple TCP segments and the final segment contained only one byte.
($$VM-Series firewalls only$$) Fixed an issue where content updates and configuration commits failed with the error message `client device phase 1 failure error`.

Added the following CLI commands to address QoS packet drops due to bursty traffic: - `debug dataplane set qos-setting qos-param qlimit 300` - `debug dataplane set qos-setting qos-param red low 50 high 90` To utilize this fix, change the parameters, disable QoS, commit changes, enable QOS, and then re-commit changes.

Fixed an issue where, after you configured a proxy server, External Dynamic Lists (EDL) and system software checks did not function concurrently. This occurred when you configured service routes for Palo Alto Networks services, which caused either EDL updates or system software checks to fail, depending on the specific service route configuration. With this fix, both EDL updates and system software checks correctly utilize the configured proxy server.
Fixed an issue where, after configuring a PBF policy rule with return address in a multi-vsys configured device, commit operations failed due to the PBF return address exceeding the maximum capacity.
Fixed an issue where the `show system environmentals power` CLI command displayed duplicate slot names and associated voltage values.

($$PA-1400 Series firewalls in HA configurations only$$) Fixed an issue where a split-brain condition occurred and HA1/HA2 links went down while upgrading when the HA configuration used dataplane interfaces for HA1 and a combination of HSCI and Ethernet interfaces for HA2.

(Firewalls in a High Availability (HA) configuration) Fixed an issue where your Firewalls experienced HA split-brain, unexpected system restarts, and the routing process repeatedly stopped responding, leading to significant disruption of production traffic. This occurred when you enabled the Advanced Routing Engine, which also caused High Availability (HA) keep-alive connections to become unavailable and an out-of-memory condition. With this fix, your Firewalls maintain stable operation after you enable the Advanced Routing Engine.

Fixed an issue where traffic was disrupted during IPSec rekey operations due to a 2 second delay in sending the DELETE message for the previous Security Association (SA) to the peer gateway after a new SA was negotiated.
Fixed an issue where running BCM counter commands from the administrative shell did not consistently return output, and commands to modify queue sizes did not take effect.
Fixed an issue where the WebUI experienced significant latency when loading the initial page after a user logged in. With this fix, the WebUI loads the initial page promptly.

(PA-7050 series firewalls in HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where a firewall in an HA configuration entered a non-functional state, which was caused by system instability and unexpected process terminations following a configuration commit, preventing the firewall from maintaining a healthy passive state. With this fix, firewalls maintain a healthy state during configuration changes.

Fixed an issue where the `useridd` process became unresponsive and restarted when attempting to dump the Host Information Profile (HIP) database via CLI while the system was actively processing HIP reports. This was caused by a lock contention. With this fix, the process now operates as expected under these conditions.

(Firewalls in an active/passive HA configuration) Fixed an issue where a passive firewall would reboot and fail to complete a configuration commit after `tund` exited multiple times during a Panorama configuration push. With this fix, configuration commits complete successfully without unexpected reboots.

# PUBLIC SUMMARY Fixed an issue where the *configd* process stopped responding after pushing configuration changes from Panorama to the firewall. # COPILOT DETAILS ## DESCRIPTION The configd process experienced repeated segmentation faults (SIGSEGV) and restarts following a commit-push operation from Panorama. The crash occurred within the `getAppIdDetails` and `pan_mgmtop_show_policy_app_details` functions, indicating an issue with how application-related configuration changes were processed during the commit. ## SYMPTOMS Continuous crashes of the configd process, leading to core file generation (e.g., `configd-*.tar.gz` and `configd-*.info` files in `/opt/panlogs/cores/`). The firewall would report configd restarts. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER The issue occurred on a firewall (specifically PA-5430) after receiving a configuration commit-push from Panorama. The crash was observed during the processing of application details within the configuration. ## IMPACT Repeated configd restarts can lead to management plane instability, preventing further configuration changes, and potentially impacting other management plane operations.

Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect user authentication with certificates from a new Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) would not succeed when Certificate Revocation List (CRL) checking was enabled. This occurred because the firewall did not properly retrieve the CRL from the new PKI's Distribution Point URL. With this fix, the firewall now successfully retrieves CRLs, allowing GlobalProtect users to authenticate correctly with certificates from new PKIs.

Fixed an issue where the system failed to alert you when indices were created before their corresponding templates loaded, which could lead to unexpected data handling. With this fix, the system now proactively identifies and alerts you to these situations.

Fixed an issue where a commit operation would fail after a PAN-OS upgrade, which occurred when the virtual system (VSYS) configuration allocator usage reached 100%. With this fix, the virtual system configuration allocator usage is managed correctly, allowing commit operations to complete successfully.

Fixed an issue where the "Block Repeated Characters" setting in Minimum Password Complexity did not prevent the use of certain repeated special characters. With this fix, the system now correctly blocks repeated special characters as configured.

Fixed an issue where, after an upgrade, Panorama displayed 0% (N/A) for Environmental and Device memory metrics under the Health tab, preventing you from viewing the expected health status of your managed devices. With this fix, Panorama now accurately displays the Environmental and Device memory health metrics for your managed firewalls.

(PA-1410 firewalls in active/passive HA configuration only) Fixed a race condition that caused the all_task process to terminate unexpectedly, which caused the firewall to become unresponsive and reboot. With this fix, the all_task process operates stably, preventing unexpected reboots.

Fixed an issue where firewalls dropped new connections due to session allocation failures, which resulted in service disruption. With this fix, firewalls no longer dropped new connections due to session allocation failures.
(PA-7500 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where session information was not being logged in the dp-monitor logs. With this fix, session information is now correctly logged.

Fixed an issue where exporting policies to PDF or CSV files from Panorama did not include all policies or resulted in out-of-order entries when using a read-only (RO) or read/write (RW) access account. With this fix, policy exports now include all policies and maintain the correct order.

Fixed an issue where certain permitted IP addresses, when pushed from a Panorama template, remained editable on the firewall web interface. With this fix, these template-managed IP addresses are no longer editable on the firewall.

Fixed an issue where SSL decryption certificates pushed from Panorama did not take effect on the managed firewalls, which required a manual override on the local firewall for the certificates to become active. With this fix, the certificates now apply as expected.

Fixed an issue where User-ID XML API requests took longer than expected to return a response, which caused the web interface and captive portal pages to respond slowly or fail to load. this occurred when sending XML API requests for IP address-to-user mapping.
Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect pre-logon tunnel session was not cleared even after the user was logged in. With this fix, the session is cleared after the session timeout expires.
($$M-700 appliances only$$) Fixed an issue where Panorama displayed an incorrect maximum recommended configuration size when performing a commit.

(PA-5450 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where tech support file generation remained stuck at 0% and would not complete when initiated from the web interface or command line interface. With this fix, tech support files generate successfully.
Fixed an issue where the firewall restarted unexpectedly due to an OOM condition after upgrading to an affected release.

Fixed an issue where configuring security policies with IP External Dynamic Lists (EDLs) across multiple Virtual Systems (vsys) would prevent commit operations from completing, which was due to an incorrect virtual system memory calculation. With this fix, commit operations complete as expected.
Fixed an issue on log collectors where **Verify Update Server Identity** was not consistently enabled and visible in the XML configuration after a configuration push from Panorama.
Fixed an issue where multiple EDL fetches were queued and did not complete.

Fixed an issue where previously committed Security policy rules were removed when a full commit was performed by a different administrator, which led to the inadvertent loss of configuration changes. With this fix, Security policy rules are retained as expected after a full commit. # COPILOT DETAILS ## DESCRIPTION When multiple administrators and automation tools performing partial commits concurrently modified the Panorama candidate configuration, a subsequent full commit by a different administrator operated on a candidate config state that did not reflect rules added by the partial commits. The full commit then removed those rules from the running configuration. ## SYMPTOMS Security policy rules added by automation partial commits were absent from the running configuration after a full commit by a different administrator. Configuration audit logs confirmed the rules were added by a partial commit and then removed by the subsequent full commit job. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER Observed on Panorama running PAN-OS 11.1.6-h23 in an environment where Ansible performed partial commits alongside manual administrators performing full commits. The candidate config visible to manually logged-in administrators intermittently did not include changes committed by automation. ## IMPACT Previously committed and active security policy rules were silently removed from the device group configuration, creating security policy gaps that went undetected until manually discovered.
Fixed an issue where the firewall rebooted unexpectedly when packet-diag logging was enabled. With this fix, the firewall maintains stability when this logging is active.

(Firewalls in active/passive HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where the running configuration incorrectly displayed an "out of sync" status and different MD5 values between HA peers, which led to misrepresentation of the synchronization state even when configuration changes were successfully applied to the passive firewall. With this fix, the synchronization status accurately reflects the configuration state between HA peers.
Fixed an issue where SNMP queries for TCP connections per second (CPS) metrics on single vsys firewalls returned inconsistent values.

Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect Portal connections would fail to authenticate when using client certificates, which occurred because the Common Name (CN) from the certificate was improperly encoded during the authentication process. With this fix, GlobalProtect correctly processes certificate Common Name (CN) usernames during authentication.

($$Firewalls in active/active HA configurations only$$) Fixed an issue where NAT failures occurred due to the IP pool not releasing unused resources in the Active Secondary firewall. This occurred because the secondary firewall attempts to release a Persistent DIPP NATed port that was originally allocated by the NAT policy from first firewall, leading to a ownership mismatch during the session teardown process.

($$PA-5450 firewalls and PA-7000 Series firewalls with 100G NPCs only$$) Fixed an issue where intermittent packet loss occurred when traversing the dataplane after upgrading the firewall. This occurred when a dataplane HA interface was configured in an environment where Slot 1 was unpopulated , which resulted in a wildcard entry being created within the QMAP table.
Fixed an issue where a data processing component would unexpectedly stop functioning under certain operational conditions. With this fix, the component now maintains stable operation.
Fixed an issue where the telemetry service or API did not return device certificate status data. With this fix, the telemetry service and API now correctly provide device certificate status.

Fixed an issue where IP mappings would remain with future timestamps, which prevented them from being visible through the command-line interface and from being cleared using standard commands. This behavior was caused by an NTP issue, which resulted in IP mappings not functioning as expected. With this fix, IP mappings are correctly managed and cleared.
Fixed an issue where SCM did not update device telemetry for the firewall after upgrading to an affected release.
Fixed an issue where the `debug management-server max-ref-xpaths 8000` CLI command was not applied automatically, and a *configd* process restart was required for the change to take effect.
Fixed an issue where Selective Push operations failed after a partial revert was performed for deleted objects in a Panorama device group, which led to invalid object references.

(Firewalls in active/passive HA configuration) Fixed an issue where the `dnsproxy` process would unexpectedly terminate, which led to an out-of-memory condition and affected network connectivity. With this fix, the `dnsproxy` process now maintains stable operation.

Fixed an issue where traffic to multiple websites intermittently encountered a block page, which occurred because traffic was incorrectly matched to a default security policy instead of the intended allow policy. With this fix, traffic is processed according to the configured security policies.

(Firewalls in active/passive HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where, after an HA failover, the new active firewall incorrectly sent a route flush for static routes redistributed into OSPF, which resulted in temporary network disruption. With this fix, the firewall properly maintained OSPF routes after an HA failover.
Fixed an issue where processes restarted and the firewall unexpectedly rebooted when you configured a Security policy rule with **Source Device > quarantine**.

Fixed an issue where users connecting to GlobalProtect were intermittently unable to access internal resources, with traffic incorrectly dropped by a block policy, which occurred despite an allow policy being configured for the traffic. With this fix, traffic is correctly evaluated against configured policies.
(PA-7080 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the Strata Logging Service (SLS/CDL) status displayed a device connectivity error erroneously.

Fixed an issue where a GlobalProtect configuration push from Panorama to a firewall would fail due to an incorrect validation that flagged DHCP IP Pool and IP Pool settings as mutually exclusive, even when these settings were configured on separate GlobalProtect gateways or not simultaneously enabled. With this fix, the validation logic correctly processes these configurations.

(Firewalls in an Active/Active HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where a discrepancy occurred between the total number of allocated sessions and the sum of active sessions on the secondary Active node. With this fix, the session counts now accurately reflect the active sessions.

Fixed an issue where the Auto Push on 1st Connect feature on Panorama did not automatically push configurations to managed firewalls upon their initial connection. This behavior occurred even when the feature was enabled, requiring a manual commit operation on Panorama to complete the configuration push. With this fix, configurations are automatically pushed as expected when a firewall connects to Panorama for the first time with the feature enabled.
Fixed an issue where the firewall rebooted unexpectedly without any configuration or power changes.

Fixed an issue where telemetry data was not sent to the cloud due to the firewall being unable to resolve the destination server's FQDN even when a proxy server was configured. With this fix, the firewall properly sends telemetry data through the configured proxy server without requiring direct public DNS resolution for the telemetry server's FQDN.

Fixed an issue where shadow rule and duplicate rule warnings did not appear during the validation stage of a configuration commit operation, which prevented administrators from addressing these issues before the final commit to the device. With this fix, these warnings now appear during the validation stage.
Fixed an issue where "Dataplane under severe load" system log is not generated when all Dataplane CPU cores reach 100%.

Fixed an issue where security policies intermittently did not apply as expected to users, which resulted in inconsistent access. This occurred because the User-ID Agent learned user identities in multiple formats, such as User Principal Name (UPN) and Security Account Manager (SAM) account names, which led to inconsistent group mapping and unreliable policy enforcement. With this fix, security policies apply consistently based on user group memberships.

(PA-7000b with LFC firewalls only) Fixed an issue where Panorama-pushed log forwarding configurations were unexpectedly removed after a PAN-OS downgrade, which caused log forwarding to stop. With this fix, Panorama-pushed configurations persist as expected after a downgrade.
Fixed an issue where SFP ports did not establish a link with a third-party peer device when forced speed was configured on the firewall and the peer device was set to `nonegotiate`.

Fixed an issue where the `set system setting target-vsys` command output displayed the virtual system (vsys) ID in both columns. With this fix, the command output now correctly displayed the vsys ID and the corresponding vsys name.

Fixed an issue where users experienced high latency spikes, packet loss, and slow application performance when decryption and HTTP/2 inspection were enabled. With this fix, performance counters are collected for further debug.

(PA-7000 Series firewalls only) Fixed an issue where firewalls displayed critical alerts indicating insufficient fantray for system components, which resulted from an incorrect interpretation of hardware status after a software upgrade. With this fix, the system accurately reports the status of hardware components.

Fixed an issue where incorrect source region information appeared in GlobalProtect logs, which occurred because the location service lookup did not consistently return region information for public IP addresses. With this fix, accurate source region information is consistently displayed.

(PA-VM firewalls only) Fixed an issue where web-browsing sessions were logged with an end-reason of 'Policy Deny' or 'Discard' even though security policies allowed the traffic, which occurred due to an error in session processing after policy rematching. With this fix, traffic logs accurately reflect the allowed status of sessions.

Fixed an issue where the firewall repeatedly restarted when the monitored User-ID server became unreachable during Kerberos authentication connection attempts, which caused the authentication process to stop responding. On firewalls in HA configurations, both peer firewalls entered maintenance mode.

Fixed an issue where your firewall, configured as a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) client, unexpectedly changed its DHCP server IP address. This resulted in the firewall receiving negative acknowledgments (NAKs) during lease renewals and using an unintended DHCP server. This occurred when the DHCP client received a second DHCP Offer from a different server after completing its initial lease acquisition process. With this fix, your firewall maintains the correct DHCP server IP address, ensuring stable lease renewals.

Fixed an issue where a system process terminated unexpectedly, which caused the device to restart and resulted in an extended service interruption. With this fix, the device maintains stable operation.

(VM-100 firewalls in FIPS mode only) Fixed an issue where SSL sessions were discarded when forward proxy decryption was enabled, which occurred when the random number generator experienced resource exhaustion under high load. With this fix, the firewall maintains SSL sessions as expected during periods of high decryption activity.
Fixed an issue where an ethernet interface remained in a down state after repeated automated enable/disable cycles and required manual intervention, which resulted in backup outages.

# PUBLIC SUMMARY Fixed an issue where FTP-DATA sessions did not match the installed predict session, which led to session termination in HA configurations. # COPILOT DETAILS ## DESCRIPTION In an active/active HA environment, after the FTP control channel created a predict session for the passive-mode FTP data connection, the HA subsystem deleted that predict session (`tracker stage l7proc: ha-delete`) before the client's SYN for the FTP data connection arrived. The incoming FTP data SYN then found no matching predict session, went through standard session setup as unknown-tcp, and was denied by policy. ## SYMPTOMS FTP data sessions were denied and appeared in the traffic log as unknown-tcp without an associated predict session. Session info for the affected predict session showed `tracker stage l7proc: ha-delete`. Global counters showed anomalous `session_predict_dst` values. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER Occurred on PA-5420 firewalls running PAN-OS 10.2.12-h4 in an active/active HA configuration with FTP passive mode. The issue occurred approximately every 30–60 minutes. ## IMPACT FTP data transfers were intermittently denied, disrupting file transfers that relied on passive-mode FTP through the firewall.

Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect authentication override cookie lifetimes were implicitly limited by the configured login lifetime, which prevented administrators from setting a longer override period. With this fix, the GlobalProtect authentication override cookie lifetime can be configured to extend beyond the login lifetime. To enable this fix, an operational command is available to revert to the previous behavior.
Fix an issue where the AI Security profile was referenced in the Security profile group, which caused the device group to remain out of sync after a selective push to devices for device groups.

Fixed an issue where the firewall intermittently failed to send a TCP Reset (RST) packet to the client when a threat was detected during an HTTPS file download with SSL decryption enabled, which resulted in sessions stalling. With this fix, the firewall now consistently sends TCP Reset packets as configured. To enable this fix, enable the following CLI command: `set session tcp-fptcp-expedite-rst yes`.
Fixed an issue where processes stopped responding unexpectedly.

(PA-VM AWS VM-SERIES-4 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the Management Plane (MP) CPU experienced high spikes during daily telemetry collection, which was caused by specific processes involved in the collection. (PA-440 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where system logs were not generated for an extended period after sequential manual restarts of management plane services, which led to the management plane entering an unresponsive state that the system's watchdog process did not detect or recover from. Fixed an issue where the system unexpectedly shut down and restarted multiple times due to an internal process repeatedly restarting. With this fix, the system no longer experiences unexpected shutdowns.

Fixed an issue where SD-WAN SaaS monitoring for HTTPS URLs continuously flapped, which caused frequent traffic shifting between ISPs. This occurred due to the firewall unexpectedly hitting resource limits for monitoring.

Fixed an issue where disabling an SD-WAN configuration on a template stack for a subinterface, after overriding the base template configuration, would result in an error. With this fix, the configuration can be disabled as expected.

Fixed an issue where an error message was displayed that an IoT Security license was required even when the firewall had a valid Enterprise IoT license, which resulted in devices not appearing under **Objects > Devices** but correctly appearing in SCM.

Fixed an issue where attempting to preview configuration changes before pushing them from Panorama to a managed firewall would fail to display the expected configuration differences. With this fix, configuration change previews now display as expected.
Fixed an issue where SWG Explicit Proxy Kerberos authentication bypass did not occur for some URLs that matched a configured URL category.

Fixed an issue where routes learned via Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) refreshed during a commit operation that did not include BGP-related changes on firewalls with Advanced Routing Engine (ARE) enabled. The issue occurred because the BGP process temporarily stopped and restarted during the commit. With this fix, BGP routes no longer refreshed during commits that did not involve BGP changes.
Fixed an issue where AWF was not honoring the Maximum Latency settings.
($$Panorama appliances in Microsoft Azure environments only$$) Fixed an issue where Panorama continuously displayed disk-related read/write errors in the console logs.
Fixed an issue where you were unable to add logging drives to the firewall, and validation errors occurred when pushing configurations from Panorama.

Fixed an issue where the CRL download failed because it followed the Service Route Setting instead of the CRL's own setting. The fix allows CRL to follow its own setting, enabling the download to succeed.

# PUBLIC SUMMARY Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect iOS users were unable to connect due to the firewall incorrectly reporting that the maximum number of users was exceeded, even when the actual number of active users was below the configured limit. # COPILOT DETAILS ## DESCRIPTION iOS clients using the native IPsec/IKEv2 VPN client generated multiple duplicate session registrations due to reconnect behavior. Each registration incremented the internal user counter in rasmgr, but the corresponding session terminations did not reliably decrement it. Over time, accumulated stale entries exhausted the configured maximum user count (1500), blocking new connection attempts. ## SYMPTOMS New iOS VPN connection attempts failed with `failed to login user ..., exceed max-user 1500` in the ikemgr-ng log despite only ~40 active users. The rasmgr log showed repeated `force-logout` events and incrementing `error-dup-user` counters for the same user. A firewall reboot temporarily resolved the issue, which then recurred after a few days. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER Observed on a PA-3410 running PAN-OS 11.2.11 with iOS native VPN clients (IPsec/IKEv2). The issue gradually accumulated over several days of normal operation. ## IMPACT iOS VPN users were unable to connect after the stale session counter reached the configured limit, requiring a firewall reboot every two to three days as a temporary workaround.

Fixed an issue where selective configuration pushes from Panorama failed after an upgrade, which caused shared policy rules to go out of sync. With this fix, selective configuration pushes complete successfully and policies remain in sync.

Fixed an issue where Panorama would change service routes configured with Loopback interfaces in templates to "Any" after an upgrade to PAN-OS 12.1.3, particularly when importing a new device. With this fix, Panorama preserves Loopback interface assignments within template configurations.

(Panorama only) Fixed an issue where the log daemon (logd) would restart periodically, which resulted in commit operations failing with a "Client logd not connected" error. This issue occurred when SD-WAN site names contained special characters or exceeded a specific length. With this fix, the log daemon remains stable and commit operations complete successfully.

Fixed an issue where the IoT (Internet of Things) License column in the Panorama user interface (UI) incorrectly displayed the status as red or 'X', which occurred when a Device Security Hub license was in use instead of a dedicated IoT license. With this fix, Panorama accurately reflects the IoT license status for Device Security Hub licenses.
Fixed an issue where botnet reports were not generated after an upgrade to PAN-OS 12.1.5.

(PA-410 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the `/opt/panlogs` partition would become full when a process crashed, which occurred because the partition was too small to accommodate the large core files generated by default. With this fix, the partition size was optimized to prevent this issue.
Fixed an issue where exporting Custom Reports to CSV failed with a `UnicodeEncodeError` message when report entries contained multibyte characters.
($$Google Cloud NGFW Enterprise VM-Series firewalls only$$) Fixed an issue where the HTTP2 threat logs did not include VPC ID, Security_key, and Endpoint ID.

Fixed an issue where TCP sessions were dropped due to an ACK-out-of-window condition during TCP reassembly when SYN cookies were enabled in a Zone Protection Profile. With this fix, TCP session establishment with SYN cookies enabled correctly tracks sequence numbers and no longer drops valid ACK packets from the Server.

Fixed an issue where a GlobalProtect gateway would not request a Host Information Profile (HIP) report from a client even when the client generated a new MD5 sum, which resulted in the firewall incorrectly determining that a new HIP report was not required and led to outdated information in the HIP match logs. With this fix, the gateway properly requests updated HIP reports when a new MD5 sum is detected.

Fixed an issue on Panorama™ appliances where previewing configuration changes before pushing them to a managed firewall timed out or displayed an internal server error when the firewall took longer than 49 seconds to generate the configuration difference (such as on lower-resource firewalls or when a large PAN-OS® version gap between Panorama and the firewall required multiple configuration transforms). With this fix, you can increase the preview timeout (49 to 240 seconds; default is 49) using the new Panorama CLI command
Fixed an issue where a system log was not generated when the proxy reached its session limit.
($$KVM VM-Series firewalls only$$) Fixed an issue where ARP entries were incomplete after an upgrade to an affected release.

Fixed an issue where network interfaces would lose Layer 2 connectivity, which resulted in internal ports being unavailable, after a software upgrade. With this fix, network interfaces maintain proper Layer 2 connectivity after an upgrade.

(Prisma Access GlobalProtect Gateways only) Fixed an issue where a deleted custom anti-spyware signature continued to block traffic after a successful commit operation, which caused the dataplane to incorrectly enforce the deleted signature. With this fix, the dataplane correctly removed deleted signatures and enforced the updated policy.

(PA-VM virtual machines only) Fixed an issue where firewalls displayed an 'EAL Ingest Connection Status: Failure' message when attempting to connect to the EAL ingest service, which occurred because the firewall encountered an error parsing certain certificates with negative serial numbers. With this fix, the firewalls successfully established connectivity to the EAL ingest service.
Fixed an issue where importing PKCS12 certificates failed with the error `Import of certificate and private-key failed. Failed to extract certificate`.
Fixed an issue where licenses were not installed after bootstrapping a VM-Series firewall in an air-gapped environment.
Fixed an issue where, after upgrading Panorama, a custom admin role with Object Level Changes disabled did not automatically populate out-of-sync firewalls in the push scope.

Fixed an issue where Panorama continued to display a message prompting a device reboot to activate changes, even after the managed device had been rebooted. This occurred after certain configuration changes, such as enabling jumbo frames, which caused the message to persist incorrectly. With this fix, the message now clears as expected after the device reboots.

Fixed an issue where the log purging process on the Panorama log collector would not complete successfully, which prevented logs from being automatically removed after their configured retention period. With this fix, logs are purged as expected according to their retention settings.

Fixed an issue where, on firewalls with QoS configured, packet buffer utilization gradually increased after a commit and did not decrease—even after a high availability (HA) failover—which required a reboot to restore normal operation. With this fix, QoS-related packet buffer resources are now properly released.

Fixed an issue where SNMPv3 (Simple Network Management Protocol version 3) traps sent by the firewall were not accepted by the monitoring server and were dropped after you changed the authentication and privacy protocols of an SNMPv3 server profile that was already in use (for example, from SHA and AES to SHA-256 and AES-256) without changing the username or engine ID. With this fix, the firewall applies the new protocols to the existing profile immediately, and the monitoring server accepts the traps.

Fixed an issue where ACE applications did not match the correct Security policy rules when the service was not set to **Application Default** after an upgrade, which caused traffic to be incorrectly denied.

(Panorama appliances only) Fixed an issue where Panorama experienced memory leaks, which occurred during repeated commit operations on the configuration. With this fix, memory usage remained stable during these operations.
Fixed an issue where the *sslmgr* process stopped responding when attempting to display the OSCP host cache.
Fixed an issue where high memory utilization occurred in the escd process. With this fix, memory utilization for the process remained stable.
Fixed an issue where memory utilization slowly increased and was not released, which involved the `configd` process. With this fix, memory is properly released.

(VM Panorama only) Fixed an issue where the `configd` process experienced a gradual increase in memory utilization, which would trigger high-memory alerts. This increase was observed during routine operations involving multiple commits. With this fix, the `configd` process maintains stable memory usage.

Fixed an issue where a selective push from Panorama to the firewall was successful even when applying rename operation failed in selective push, which resulted in configurations on the firewall being deleted. With this fix, the selective push will fail when applying rename operation fails.

Fixed an issue where enabling multi-vsys on a firewall with shared override nodes created duplicate configuration nodes, which caused commit operations to fail. With this fix, enabling multi-vsys no longer duplicates configuration nodes.
Fixed an issue where high CPU utilization occurred on one of the CPU cores.

Fixed an issue where a Security policy rule configured in the Shared device group on Panorama was not displayed in the web interface for a child device group, which caused a discrepancy between the displayed configuration and the actual deployed configuration on the associated device. With this fix, the user interface accurately reflects the deployed security policy rules.

(PA-550 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where firewalls experienced unexpected reboots after a High Availability (HA) failover, which led to a loss of network connectivity. With this fix, firewalls maintain stability and network connectivity during and after HA failover operations.

Fixed an issue where clicking OK in the Panorama™ user interface when viewing a WildFire® cluster configuration inadvertently removed the cluster management and high availability (HA) configuration on the cluster interfaces, even without making changes. With this fix, the configuration is retained as expected.
Fixed an issue where a corrupted entry in mongodb caused the configd crash when XML API set operations were called

Fixed an issue where the firewall was unable to revert locally overridden configurations for permitted IP addresses on the management interface after an upgrade. With this fix, the configuration could be reverted as expected.

Fixed an issue where a Virtual Private Network (VPN) tunnel failed to automatically re-establish when the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) gateway peer's Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) resolved to a new IP address. This occurred even when DNS resolution correctly provided the updated IP address, which prevented the tunnel from coming back online without manual intervention. Fixed an issue where IP addresses configured for Source Address Exclusions in a Zone Protection Profile within a template stack did not save correctly. With this fix, the IP addresses save as expected.

Fixed an issue where critical alerts related to registered IP address updates appeared in system logs even when User-ID was not configured due to a conflict during simultaneous updates of IP tags and EDLs. To enable this fix, run the CLI command `debug user-id regip-max-update-retry rate <value>` with a value between 30 and 300.

Fixed an issue where the firewall experienced high management plane memory utilization, which led to inaccessibility of the management interfaces (Web GUI, CLI, and console), disconnection from the High Availability (HA) cluster, and repeated reboot cycles. This behavior occurred after attempting to upgrade the PAN-OS software and applying or restoring the firewall configuration. With this fix, the firewall maintains stability and completes software upgrades successfully.
Fixed an issue where log forwarding stopped. With this fix, log forwarding resumes normal operation.

Fixed an issue where a **Commit and Push** operation on Panorama did not successfully push configuration changes to Prisma Access endpoints. This occurred when the system reported that not all commit jobs were triggered. With this fix, **Commit and Push** operations now correctly apply configurations to Prisma Access.
Fixed an issue where BFD sessions did not reestablish on the newly elected leader after a leader failover event that occurred when the previous leader node was suspended.

Fixed an issue where user-ID mappings for a user were incorrectly cleared during a user group synchronization event when the user was removed from one group before being added to another. With this fix, user-ID mappings are correctly updated during group changes.

($$Firewalls in active/passive HA configurations only$$) Fixed an issue where firewalls repeatedly entered an initialization and suspended state due to changes in a backend URL. With this fix, the firewalls maintained their active state.

Fixed an issue where the web interface did not display the file name and location for custom response pages after a successful upload. With this fix, the web interface correctly displays the details of uploaded custom response pages.

Fixed an issue where access to websites was interrupted or pages rendered incompletely when SSL/TLS decryption was enabled due to the firewall prematurely terminating sessions upon receiving a **TLS Close Notify** alert. Fixed an issue where tunnel interfaces could not establish connectivity when advanced routing was enabled, which resulted in an inability to ping between satellite and gateway tunnel interfaces. With this fix, tunnel interface communication functions as expected with advanced routing enabled.

Fixed an issue where firewalls experienced continuous unexpected restarts and entered a suspended state due to improper processing of certain URLs. With this fix, firewalls maintain stable operation in HA configurations.

Fixed an issue where traffic did not hit Security policy rules configured with a HIP profile even when the HIP match log indicated a successful match. This occurred after upgrading and importing a configuration.

Fixed an issue on the web interface where HA related filter options (**HA Cluster ID**, **HA Cluster State**, and **HA Pair Status**) disappeared from the **Commit > Push to Devices > Edit Selection**) window in Panorama when the window was reopened within the same login session. Fixed an issue where the dataplane silently dropped HTTP POST payloads, which disrupted application integrations. This occurred due to an internal error when processing XFF headers within the CTD engine.

Fixed an issue where firewalls did not generate system logs when an administrator cleared logs, which impacted auditing capabilities. With this fix, firewalls now generate system logs for log clearing events.

Fixed an intermittent issue where firewall restarted unexpectedly while processing zip files.

Fixed an issue where the management interface incorrectly displayed a Power over Ethernet (PoE) icon for an aggregate Ethernet subinterface that was not a PoE-capable port. With this fix, the interface displays the correct link state.
Fixed an issue where Panorama or Firewall did not automatically resume syslog forwarding over TCP after the syslog server became unavailable or was restarted.

(PA-5250 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the in-flight monitoring feature would not activate or generate diagnostic logs as expected when specific conditions were met, which prevented the system from capturing information about packet buffer and on-chip descriptor spikes. With this fix, the in-flight monitoring feature now functions correctly.

(PA-520, PA-545-POE, PA-555-POE, PA-550 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where a commit operation would fail, which was caused by incorrectly updated capacity numbers. With this fix, commit operations complete successfully.

Fixed an issue where the Panorama web interface showed blank Host Information Profile (HIP) Match log entries when opened in Detailed Log View. With this fix, the Detailed Log View now displays the expected information for HIP Match logs.

Fixed an issue where the cellular interface did not come up and entered a **Dead Zone** state after an upgrade due to the management plane losing communication with the modem hardware. With this fix, the cellular interface came up by having an expected APN name based on the SIM card carrier.
(PA-400 Series Firewalls) Fixed an issue where firewalls rebooted unexpectedly after an upgrade. With this fix, firewalls now operate stably after an upgrade.

Fixed an issue where the Panorama Monitor tab and CLI output were blank and Elasticsearch entered a restart loop, which occurred after upgrading Panorama to a specific PAN-OS version. With this fix, Elasticsearch operates stably, and log data displays correctly in the Monitor tab and CLI.
Fixed an issue where the firewall experienced unexpected process terminations, which resulted in an HA failover and led to the dataplane becoming unresponsive.

(PA-5440 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where traffic designated for no decryption was unexpectedly denied due to a certificate validation error. With this fix, traffic designated for no decryption is processed as expected.

Fixed an issue where multicast routing entries for certain IPTV streams were not correctly installed or populated with necessary interface information, which prevented the proper forwarding of multicast traffic. With this fix, multicast traffic now forwards as expected.

Fixed an issue where the push scope window did not display the target devices when attempting to push configurations from Panorama, which required manual selection of templates or device groups. With this fix, the push scope window now correctly populates with the intended push scope.
Fixed an issue where a Strata Logging Service license showed as failing to install even though it was successfully fetched.
($$OCTEON, MIPS, platforms only$$) Fixed an issue where the dataplane became unresponsive. With this fix, the dataplane operates stably.

(PA-VM firewalls only) Fixed an issue where registered IP-Tag mappings did not correctly populate Dynamic Address Group (DAG) membership after an upgrade, which caused security policy rule mismatches and traffic to be incorrectly dropped.
