Fixed an issue where the `configd` process on Panorama unexpectedly stopped when a search was performed within the post-rule security policy. With this fix, the `configd` process now maintains stability during such searches.
Fixed an issue where the characters in PDF Summary Reports did not display correctly when the Locale was set as Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese.

Fixed an issue where testing an SCP server connection from the Panorama web interface returned an error instead of prompting to allow the host key, which prevented the successful establishment of the connection. With this fix, the system now correctly prompts to allow the host key.
Fixed an issue where a memory leak associated with some display CLI commands caused instability.

(AWS VM-Series firewalls in active/passive HA configuration with interface move mode) Fixed an issue where data plane interfaces did not acquire DHCP IP addresses after an HA failover, which prevented proper network connectivity. With this fix, interfaces correctly obtained IP addresses.
Fixed an issue where commit operations failed due to redis *idmgr* connection leaks. With this fix, commit operations complete as expected.

Fixed an issue where SNMPv3 communication would fail after an upgrade from PAN-OS 11.1 to PAN-OS 12.1.6 when using SHA-512 authentication and AES-256 privacy. With this fix, SNMPv3 communication functions as expected after the upgrade.

Fixed an issue where enabling App Acceleration resulted in connectivity disruption for GlobalProtect users and branches connected through ION devices, which prevented access to applications. With this fix, App Acceleration functions as expected without causing connectivity issues.

(M-200 firewalls in active/passive HA configuration) Fixed an issue where Panorama did not automatically resume log forwarding to a syslog server over TCP after the server became available, which required manual intervention to restore logging. With this fix, log forwarding resumes automatically.

(PA-460 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) sessions were incorrectly associated with an unexpected user in traffic logs, which occurred because the Application Layer Gateway (ALG) for SIP incorrectly inherited user identity for predicted sessions. With this fix, SIP traffic correctly uses the established IP-to-user mapping.

($$VM-Series firewalls in AWS Cloud Mode with Geneve-based service chaining$$) Fixed an issue where the firewall experienced unexpected reboots and a temporary loss of connectivity. This occurred when the *mprelay* process attempted to process system object modifications involving Geneve service chain metadata, which led to repeated process interruptions and a system reboot. With this fix, the firewall now handles these operations without interruption.

($$VM-Series firewalls in Microsoft Azure environments integrated with Azure Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)$$) Fixed an issue where SSL decryption did not function correctly for connections when the accumulation proxy was enabled, which caused the firewall to send an ACK packet through an incorrect tunnel. With this fix, SSL decryption operates as expected.

# PUBLIC SUMMARY Fixed an issue where the firewall unexpectedly terminated operations and rebooted due to an internal software error. # COPILOT DETAILS ## DESCRIPTION The `pan_task` dataplane process (along with `all_task`) terminated with signal 11 (SIGSEGV) due to a general protection fault. Multiple core files were generated across several all_task instances, and the recovery mechanism triggered a full firewall reboot. ## SYMPTOMS System log showed `kernel: traps: pan_task[13599] general protection fault`. The md_apps.log recorded `Process comm exited with signal of 11; core dumped: yes` followed by `Process all_task_1 exited with signal of 11; core dumped: yes`. The firewall rebooted without any administrative action. ## CONDITIONS/TRIGGER Observed on a PA-VM running PAN-OS 11.1.6-h23. The incident occurred without any known configuration change or traffic event at the time of the fault. ## IMPACT The unexpected reboot caused an unplanned network outage, interrupting all traffic passing through the firewall until it completed the restart sequence.

Fixed an issue where local commits continued to report an inflated merged configuration size and trigger configuration size warnings after a firewall was migrated from Panorama™ management to local management. This occurred because residual Panorama-pushed configuration data was still included when calculating the configuration size summary in the commit status message. With this fix, the commit message accurately reports the total configuration size (local and predefined) after migration.

(PA-220 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where predefined reports were inconsistent and returned "no matching records", which resulted in the reports not being generated as expected. With this fix, predefined reports are generated consistently.

Fixed an issue where the Panorama web interface did not display all available Cloud Services Plugin update versions after checking for updates. With this fix, all available plugin versions display correctly.

Fixed an issue where, with software cut-through enabled (the default), a long-lived session continued forwarding traffic to an Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) entry after that entry was released and reassigned to a different host. As a result, traffic such as Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) was delivered to an unintended destination, which prevented sessions from establishing. With this fix, the firewall forwards traffic to the correct destination after an ARP entry is reassigned.

(Software firewalls on T2 instances with 16GB memory and 16 vCPUs in a maximum configuration) Fixed an issue where the total memory headroom was reduced in specific software versions. With this fix, the memory headroom is maintained as expected.
Fixed an issue where auto-commit operations would fail during boot-up or after a reboot. With this fix, auto-commit operations complete as expected.

Fixed an issue where User-ID distribution experienced delays, which occurred due to congestion in the Host Information Profile (HIP) report queue. With this fix, User-ID information distributes without delay.

Fixed an issue where the firewall incorrectly routed DNS traffic from the management interface instead of the configured service route interface when an address object was set as the source address. With this fix, DNS traffic now correctly uses the designated service route interface.
Fixed an issue where IPsec tunnels frequently went down due to high process memory utilization. With this fix, the system process now manages memory correctly, preventing tunnel instability.

Fixed an issue where the `show object registered-ip` command ignored the tag filter when the `start-point` parameter was also used, which caused the command to return the complete, unfiltered registered-IP runtime database from the specified offset. With this fix, the command now correctly applies the tag filter when used with the start-point parameter.

(VM-Series firewalls in Azure deployments) Fixed an issue where intermittent traffic denial occurred when the 'Strip X-Forwarded-For' feature was enabled, which caused the firewall to truncate X-Forwarded-For (XFF) IP addresses by dropping the first digit. The firewall then used this truncated IP address during App-ID re-identification, leading to security policy mismatches and implicit denials. With this fix, XFF headers are processed correctly, preventing IP truncation and ensuring proper policy evaluation.

Fixed an issue where commit validation on Panorama unexpectedly applied template configuration changes to the firewall, which led to an outage of FQDN resolution. With this fix, commit validation no longer alters firewall behavior.

Fixed an issue where addresses configured in a Policy-Based Forwarding (PBF) policy were removed, which led to an outage, when a node was added to a region and then immediately removed before full provisioning. With this fix, addresses in PBF policies remain stable during node operations.

(PA-5450 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where session information was not displayed properly in the show session id <session-id> output when you used a session ID obtained from the show running resource-monitor ingress-backlogs output, which occurred when the firewall processed heavy traffic. With this fix, the session information displays as expected.

Fixed an issue where traffic for certain websites was incorrectly matched to a security policy, preventing access for users when using specific web browsers, which occurred because the firewall used a generic session category for policy matching. With this fix, traffic correctly matches the intended security policy.
Fixed an issue where an internal system user account, used for telemetry operations, was not recognized as a valid user. With this fix, the system properly recognizes the account.
Fixed an issue where using the `scp-server-connection` command would cause the system to become unresponsive. With this fix, the command now functions as expected.

(Firewalls in active/passive HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where DHCP clients on interfaces remained in a rebooting state long after a device reboot or failover, which was caused by a race condition. With this fix, DHCP clients properly acquired IP addresses after reboots or failovers.

Fixed an issue where a commit to add a new tunnel interface to an existing Virtual Router caused BGP routes to be temporarily withdrawn, which led to active traffic sessions being routed over incorrect paths during the commit window. With this fix, adding a tunnel interface to an existing Virtual Router no longer disrupts BGP route availability.

(Prisma Access GlobalProtect gateway nodes) Fixed an issue where commit operations experienced significant delays, which occurred because a configuration parsing process stalled during commit. With this fix, commit operations complete within expected timeframes.

Fixed an issue where predefined PDF summary reports were not generated on firewalls and Panorama Report Appliances, which occurred because the underlying report generation process was unexpectedly rejected. With this fix, predefined PDF summary reports are generated as expected.
Fixed an issue where the proxy generated HTTP 503 errors for multiple URLs, which prevented users from connecting to servers. With this fix, the proxy now functions as expected.
Fixed an issue where a RAID array could not be rebuilt after a disk replacement because the data copy operation timed out. With this fix, RAID array rebuild operations complete successfully.

Fixed an issue where multicast traffic did not forward on the first attempt after migration to the Advanced Routing Engine (ARE) with multicast buffering enabled, which caused traffic to flow only on subsequent attempts. With this fix, the firewall now forwards or buffers the first multicast packet as expected.

(Firewalls in an active/passive HA configuration only) Fixed an issue where commit operations failed or stalled, and the `useridd` process consumed 100% CPU and became unresponsive. This occurred due to ID manager exhaustion, which prevented configuration changes and degraded User-ID functionality. With this fix, commit operations complete successfully, and `useridd` functions as expected.
Fixed an issue where firewalls intermittently disconnected from SLS. With this fix, firewalls maintained a stable connection to SLS.

Fixed an issue where a telemetry settings banner continued to display on the firewall even after the device was removed from its Tenant Service Group (TSG) association, which indicated that the device was still managed by Strata Cloud Manager (SCM). With this fix, the banner no longer appeared after the device was disassociated from the TSG.
(PA-VM firewalls only) Fixed an issue where the firewall unexpectedly rebooted, which occurred during Geneve protocol traffic processing. With this fix, the firewall operates stably.

(PA-1410 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where disk checks incorrectly targeted the SDA partition instead of the NVMe partition, which resulted in an unexpected FSCK status for the `pancfg` partition and caused devices to boot into maintenance mode. With this fix, disk checks correctly target the NVMe partition.

(Firewalls performing ZTP over cellular connections) Fixed an issue where certificate fetching failed during Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) over cellular connections, which occurred when the firewall did not correctly process the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) negotiated by the cellular carrier. With this fix, certificate fetching completes successfully over cellular connections.
[PA-54xx only] Fixed an issue where firewalls experienced reduced performance during application identification. With this fix, application identification performance is restored.
Fixed an issue where device telemetry uploads would fail, which led to critical alerts in the system logs. With this fix, telemetry data uploads complete successfully.

(PA-5450 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) negotiation would not establish on the active firewall after a PAN-OS upgrade. With this fix, LACP negotiation establishes as expected.

Fixed an issue where traffic failed to match security policies that referenced Active Directory (AD) groups by their short names after a firewall reboot. This occurred when the number of fetched AD groups exceeded the platform's ID Manager capacity, which prevented the conversion of group short names to distinguished names during the automatic commit process. With this fix, the system correctly converts group short names to distinguished names during the automatic commit process, allowing policies to match traffic as expected.

Fixed an issue where the graphical user interface (GUI) displayed an incorrect count of blocked categories for User Credential Submission in the default URL filtering profile and in unedited URL filtering profiles copied from the default profile. With this fix, the GUI now accurately reflects the number of blocked categories.
Fixed an issue on the panorama where log filtering did not work as expected.

(Firewalls in an active/passive HA configuration) Fixed an issue where Panorama policy pushes to a passive HA firewall would intermittently revert due to a Panorama connectivity check failure, which occurred because the firewall did not restore connectivity to the Secondary Panorama in time after a commit operation. With this fix, Panorama policy pushes complete as expected.

(Firewalls with Config Selection Criteria (CSC) enabled) Fixed an issue where Authentication Override failed to regenerate a new Gateway authentication override cookie when an expired cookie already existed and Config Selection Criteria (CSC) with client certificate matching was enabled, which resulted in the Portal not generating a new cookie even after successful user authentication and CSC evaluation. With this fix, the Portal now correctly generates a new Authentication Override cookie after successful authentication and Config Selection Criteria (CSC) evaluation, ensuring clients receive a valid cookie.

Fixed an issue where during the migration of SC3 keys to a new Panorama, the Certificate Authority (CA) keys on managed firewalls were wiped, which prevented the firewalls from connecting to the Panorama. With this fix, the SC3 key migration process properly preserves CA keys, allowing managed firewalls to connect as expected.

Fixed an issue where Panorama commit and push operations did not include configuration changes made by other administrators when those administrators were selected in the 'Admin Scope Selection' option, which resulted in those changes not being pushed to firewalls. With this fix, Panorama correctly processes and pushes all selected administrator changes during commit and push operations.

Fixed an issue where communication with Microsoft Azure services was disrupted, which resulted in application outages. This occurred when firewalls dropped SYN-ACK packets that were part of a SYN-ACK cookie mechanism activated by Azure's DDoS mitigation. With this fix, firewalls now maintain connectivity during such traffic events.

Fixed an issue where traffic matched an incorrect security rule and was denied after a policy recompilation issue, which occurred during an External Dynamic List (EDL) refresh. With this fix, policy recompilation completes successfully, ensuring traffic matches the correct security rules.

(PA-5440 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where threat logs were not persistently visible and the threat prevention database was repeatedly deleted shortly after installation, which resulted in the loss of real-time threat detection and inspection. With this fix, the threat prevention database remains persistently installed and threat logs are continuously visible.

(Panorama in FIPS mode only) Fixed an issue where API key generation failed, which occurred because the system used an unsupported cryptographic padding mode for API key encryption. With this fix, API keys are generated successfully.

(PA-VM firewalls in an Azure environment with 3 data plane interfaces in an HA configuration) Fixed an issue where the Accelerated Networking status was incorrectly displayed as disabled on a data plane interface of a passive virtual machine after a reboot, which occurred when the Data Plane Development Kit (DPDK) was disabled. With this fix, the Accelerated Networking status is reported accurately.

Few configs which pushed from SCM to firewall were causing the firewall to loose its internet connectivity and the firewall wasn't able to connect to cloud and was getting stuck at discovery stage retrying indefinitely without returning failure. And now ACR performs the the config rollback once the 5 cloud connectivity check attempts failed.

Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect clients would fail to obtain a private IP address during configuration loading, which prevented successful connections when Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) was enabled. With this fix, GlobalProtect clients can successfully obtain private IP addresses.

(VM-300 firewalls deployed behind AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) with GENEVE encapsulation only) Fixed an issue where firewalls would simultaneously crash during a configuration commit, which resulted in a complete traffic outage. With this fix, firewalls remain operational during configuration commits in this environment.

(Panorama appliances only) Fixed an issue where the system was unable to add new RAID disks to existing arrays, which resulted in disk pairs remaining in a degraded state. The system would detect the drives but would not properly initialize them for inclusion in the RAID array. With this fix, the system now correctly initializes and adds new RAID disks, allowing for proper array rebuilds.
Fixed an issue where the firewall introduced out-of-order packet delivery for certain data streams, which resulted in clients receiving data in an incorrect sequence.

(RN-HP firewalls only) Fixed an issue where packet buffer resources would leak during a temporary surge in packet buffer usage, which caused tunnels to become unavailable. With this fix, packet buffer resources are managed correctly during periods of high usage.

(PA-VM firewalls only) Fixed an issue where multiple user sessions were terminated unexpectedly due to resource unavailability, which caused traffic disruption. With this fix, the firewall maintained resource stability, preventing such unexpected session terminations.

Fixed an issue where a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) session would remain in an IDLE state after its local interface or IP address was modified. With this fix, BGP sessions establish correctly after such configuration changes.
Fixed an issue where DHCPv6 relay failed on sub-interfaces when the Advanced Routing Engine was in use with DHCP IPv4 and IPv6 enabled.

Fixed an issue where syslog forwarding profiles on Log Collectors would stop sending data, which led to inconsistent log forwarding until a configuration push was performed. With this fix, syslog forwarding operates as expected without requiring manual intervention.

Fixed an issue where cloning a security rule in Policy Optimizer failed when the new rule name included '-1' appended to the original name. This occurred because the system incorrectly identified the new rule name as identical to the original, which prevented the rule from being created. With this fix, rule cloning proceeds as expected.

(All firewalls and panorama deployments that include syslog clients in logrcvr/logd) Fixed an issue where traffic logs were not forwarded to CloudWatch. With this fix, traffic logs are forwarded as expected.

(Panorama-VM) Fixed an issue where adding an interface to a logical router on Panorama via the interface configuration removed other interfaces from the logical router, which occurred when the interface was added through the interface configuration rather than the logical router configuration. With this fix, interfaces are retained as expected.

Fixed an issue where GlobalProtect IPSec connections would not successfully fall back to SSL when the IPSec connection became unavailable, which caused the system to reject the SSL fallback if it occurred too quickly. With this fix, SSL fallback functions as expected.

(PA-VM firewalls on Microsoft Hyper-V operating in Packet MMAP mode only) Fixed an issue where firewalls would unexpectedly reboot, which occurred when an internal health monitoring process incorrectly detected a critical condition. With this fix, firewalls maintain stability.

(PA-7050 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where packet capture operations on the firewall would not complete and management plane access was significantly slow. With this fix, packet capture operations now complete successfully and management plane access is responsive.

(Panorama appliances in FIPS mode) Fixed an issue where disk space on the root partition rapidly filled due to excessive logging by the log indexing process when it encountered malformed data. This issue also prevented disk cleanup operations from completing successfully. With this fix, the log indexing process handles data gracefully, and disk cleanup functions as expected.

Fixed an issue where syslog server connections would remain in an ESTABLISHED state after a commit operation when syslog forwarding was configured using TCP, which indicated a connection socket leak. With this fix, connections are properly closed.

Fixed an issue where the Managed Devices Summary page on Panorama did not display commit state, shared policy, and template information on initial load after an upgrade. With this fix, the information now displays correctly without requiring a manual page refresh.

Fixed an issue where newly deployed firewalls or otherwise would temporarily disconnect from Panorama daily at a specific time after a Panorama upgrade. These disconnections lasted for approximately 30 seconds. With this fix, firewalls maintain continuous connectivity to Panorama.

(PA-5410 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where a device unexpectedly rebooted, which occurred when the dataplane encountered an unexpected condition during URL policy processing. With this fix, the device maintains stability during URL policy processing.

(Panorama appliances only) Fixed an issue where tracebacks appeared in the `raid.log` file, accompanied by messages indicating that a redundant array of independent disks (RAID) pair had disappeared. This occurred due to an internal processing error when handling RAID device paths during system boot, which could lead to incorrect reporting of RAID status. With this fix, the system correctly processes RAID device paths, preventing these log errors and ensuring accurate RAID status.

Fixed an issue where enabling Certificate Revocation List (CRL) checking for a certificate profile prevented the system from locating the certificate profile, which caused IPsec tunnel authentication to fail. With this fix, the system correctly located the certificate profile, allowing IPsec tunnels to establish successfully.

(PA-VM firewalls in an air-gapped setup only) Fixed an issue where antivirus signature exceptions could not be added after upgrading to PAN-OS 11.1.11 or later. With this fix, antivirus signature exceptions can now be added as expected.

Fixed an issue where system disk space was rapidly consumed by a log file, and attempts to clear disk space using the cleanup command would not complete. This occurred when internal logging processes encountered data processing errors, which led to continuous log generation and prevented successful disk cleanup operations. With this fix, system logging processes handle data errors gracefully, and disk cleanup operations function as expected.

(VM-Series firewalls using the Panorama Software Licensing plugin) Fixed an issue where logs displayed an incorrect device name with an appended placeholder suffix, which occurred because the firewall's runtime state incorrectly populated the ESXi hostname field with a placeholder value. With this fix, device names in logs now display correctly without the appended suffix.

Fixed an issue where every commit on a firewall configured for IoT devices triggered Host Information Profile (HIP) match logging, which incorrectly generated vulnerability alerts based on IoT verdicts received from the IoT Security service. With this fix, the firewall no longer generated erroneous HIP match logs for IoT devices after a commit.

Fixed an issue where firewalls intermittently lost their connection to the Strata Logging Service, which caused logging to stop until the connection was re-established. With this fix, firewalls maintain a stable connection to the Strata Logging Service.

Fixed an issue where a commit to add a new tunnel interface to an existing Virtual Router caused BGP routes to be temporarily withdrawn, which led to active traffic sessions being routed over incorrect paths during the commit window. With this fix, adding a tunnel interface to an existing Virtual Router no longer disrupts BGP route availability.

(Panorama VM) Fixed an issue where address objects referenced exclusively in Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peer configurations within a template or template stack were incorrectly flagged as unused, which led to commit validation or push failures on managed firewalls when the "Share Unused Address and Service Objects with Devices" setting was disabled. With this fix, Panorama correctly recognized these address objects as active dependencies and included them in the compiled XML payload during a push.

Fixed an issue where the firewall initiated an unexpected outbound session from an internal port when an inbound TCP SYN did not complete its 3-way handshake and the ingress zone's Zone Protection Profile (ZPP) was configured to allow non-SYN TCP, which resulted in the firewall exposing an internal source port. With this fix, the firewall no longer initiated these unexpected sessions.

(PA-5430 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where web proxy sessions dropped after reaching 40,000 concurrent sessions, which occurred due to a discrepancy between the configured maximum connection value and the value used at runtime. With this fix, the maximum connection values align, preventing unexpected session termination.

Fixed an issue where the GlobalProtect Offload proxy falsely denied the initial Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 connection when client certificate authentication was in use and application data arrived with the handshake. With this fix, the proxy correctly processed these connections.

(PA-5220 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where BGP-to-OSPF and OSPF-to-BGP route redistribution stopped after a configuration commit under the Logical Router, which caused OSPF routes to take an extended period to stabilize. With this fix, route redistribution functions as expected after configuration commits.

Fixed an issue where the system encountered a parsing error for the Authority Key Identifier (AKID) extension in certificates, which prevented the AKID from being correctly processed when it began with a specific value. With this fix, the AKID extension is now correctly parsed and processed.

Fixed an issue where the Panorama™ management plane would stall during bulk configuration provisioning via the XML API when the configuration contained a large number of tag associations, which occurred because of the overhead involved in resolving tag and member references against the in-memory configuration tree. With this fix, the management plane processes such configurations more efficiently.

(PA-5420 firewalls in active/passive High Availability (HA) configuration only) Fixed an issue where the Forwarding Information Base (FIB) would become stale after HA failover events, routine configuration commits, or Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) toggles, which led to traffic blackholing. This occurred due to connection refusals between the routing control plane and the forwarding plane. With this fix, routing entries are reliably synchronized to the forwarding plane.

(PA-5570 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where traffic logs were not displayed and no data appeared in the Application Command Center (ACC). With this fix, traffic logs and ACC data display as expected.

(PA-5440 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where SaaS applications were incorrectly blocked even when a higher-order security rule should have allowed the traffic, which occurred due to an unexpected policy rematch behavior. With this fix, security policy rules are correctly applied during policy rematch, ensuring expected traffic flow.

Fixed an issue where sessions were prematurely terminated due to resource unavailability, which occurred even when the platform had not reached its capacity limits. This issue was observed when decryption was enabled for traffic from multiple remote network sites. With this fix, sessions now utilize available resources correctly and are not prematurely terminated.

(PA-520 series firewalls only) Fixed an issue where, when performing SSL Forward Proxy decryption, users experienced issues accessing websites over HTTP/HTTPS traffic and received certificate errors, which occurred because software memory pools became depleted and prevented memory allocation for proxy and L7 miscellaneous processes. With this fix, memory resources are managed correctly, allowing uninterrupted access to web services.

(PA-5440 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where inline Data Loss Prevention (DLP) forwarding experienced near-complete disruption, which resulted from internal resource exhaustion. With this fix, inline DLP forwarding operates as expected under production load.
(PA-5440 firewalls only) Fixed a null pointer issue that caused heartbeat failures and data plane instability, which resulted in unexpected firewall restarts and temporary network outages.

(HA active/passive PA-3430 firewalls using the Advanced Routing Engine (ARE)) Fixed an issue where IPv6 prefixes were not advertised between OSPFv3 areas, which occurred because an OSPFv3 Area Range configuration overlapped with ASBR loopback addresses, preventing the generation of necessary Link-State Advertisements (LSAs), and because attempts to configure route redistribution in Strata Cloud Manager (SCM) failed due to a schema validation error. With this fix, IPv6 prefixes are correctly advertised between OSPFv3 areas, and route redistribution can be configured successfully in SCM.

(PA-5420 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where OSPFv3 routes were not established on a peer device because the firewall incorrectly handled route tags during advertisement. With this fix, route tags are handled correctly.

Fixed an issue where Panorama push operations failed to firewalls running PAN-OS 12.1.7-h3 or 12.1.8, which occurred because a required module for a Hybrid SWG push script was not found during the commit process. With this fix, Panorama push operations complete successfully.

Fixed an issue where the licensing message on the Security Profiles page does not list Advanced Threat Prevention Plus as a valid license option firewalls without a Threat Prevention or Advanced Threat Prevention license. The message references only Threat Prevention and Advanced Threat Prevention, which may cause confusion for customers who have an Advanced Threat Prevention Plus add-on.

Fixed an issue where the Inline Cloud Analysis tab does not appear in the Vulnerability Protection profile in the web interface on firewalls licensed exclusively with the Advanced Threat Prevention Plus add-on. The Advanced Threat Prevention Plus license is a unified license that enables Threat Prevention and Advanced Threat Prevention features, as well as Frontier Virtual Patching, but the web interface does not recognize it as a valid entitlement for the Inline Cloud Analysis configuration. The underlying Inline Cloud Analysis functionality is not affected, however, the web interface tab is unavailable for configuration.

Fixed an issue where Management Plane memory utilization increased rapidly, which led to out-of-memory events, high availability failovers, and restarts of Management Plane processes. With this fix, Management Plane memory utilization remains stable

Fixed an issue where Anti-virus content packages do not appear under Device > Dynamic Updates when you select Check Now on firewalls licensed exclusively with an Advanced Threat Prevention Plus add-on. The web interface does not check for or display available Anti-virus updates because it does not recognize the Advanced Threat Prevention Plus license as a valid entitlement for Anti-virus content.

(PA-3400 Series firewalls only) Fixed an issue where Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) static route redistribution into Area 0 failed on an Area Border Router (ABR), which prevented the proper advertisement of routes from a Not-So-Stubby Area (NSSA) into the OSPF backbone area and resulted in subnets becoming unreachable. With this fix, route redistribution functions as expected.
Fixed a timing issue that caused the Ethernet/HSCI port to remain in a DOWN state after a physical fiber reconnection or system reboot. The port now properly recovers to an UP state after the fix.

(PA-5500 Series firewalls only) Fixed an issue where an internal interface briefly went down and reinitialized due to an incorrect link-status reading, causing the firewall to restart unexpectedly. This occurred during bursts of high network traffic, such as spikes in TLS 1.3 sessions. With this fix, the firewall verifies link status accurately before reinitializing the interface.

(PA-7500 firewalls only) Fixed an issue where NAT64 server-to-client traffic failed on sessions using hardware session offload, causing the firewall to translate the destination port incorrectly after a session was offloaded and resetting the connection. With this fix, NAT64 translates server-to-client traffic correctly on sessions using hardware session offload.

Fixed an issue where selectively disabling offload for filtered traffic did not function as expected, and sessions continued to be offloaded. With this fix, offload is correctly disabled for filtered traffic.
Fixed an issue where NAT64 client-to-server (c2s) packet IP addresses were corrupted during 6-to-4 translation after hardware offload.
Fixed an issue where a race condition prevented Certificate Signing Request (CSR) operations from completing successfully. With this fix, CSR operations complete reliably.
